name: Uniqode
summary: Dynamic QR codes and digital business cards with real-time scan analytics — connect offline touchpoints to measurable results and capture leads.
best_for: marketing teams that need dynamic QR codes with real analytics and enterprise compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001, optional HIPAA)
skip_if: you only need the occasional static QR code: a free generator does that, and Bitly is better if link-shortening is your main job
honest_knock: The tier jumps are steep and a lot is gated: analytics are capped at 60 days on the entry plan, scan limits apply across all tiers, and custom domains sit behind higher pricing. It's a real QR platform, but overkill if you just want the occasional code.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-28 on their own pricing page, read both as plain HTML and as a live browser render) The plan cards are rendered in the browser and carry no price in either reading, so what we can hold Uniqode to is its own pricing FAQ on that page, read 13 September 2026. Static QR codes are free and there is no limit on how many you create; dynamic QR codes start at a stated minimum of $9/month. NEW since our August reading: the FAQ now prices one named tier, Core at $49/month, which it calls the best value -- it does not say where Core sits in the Starter, Lite, Pro, Plus and Business+ ladder the same FAQ uses elsewhere. A custom domain is a Plus add-on at $2,000 per domain per year. Your first digital business card is free, with extra seats on a Team plan at $6 per user per month; Business+ card pricing is custom. There is a 14-day free trial, and when it expires the dynamic codes made during it go inactive while static codes keep working (without account access). Billing is annual only, in USD, invoice billing is Business+ only, and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee. Third-party listings quote a $5 entry tier; that is not what Uniqode's own page says, and we are not repeating a Lite or Pro figure we could not read at the source.

price_history.method: Stable = every amount on the vendor's pricing page identical across >= 3 of our reads over >= 30 days. A change is listed only after we confirmed the new price on the page, with a verbatim quote. Differences in raw readings are never published on their own.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We created two dynamic website QR codes, exported the list to CSV, downloaded a QR image and read the analytics page. We did not open the checkout.
findings: The sidebar counted the 14-day trial down ('Your QR Codes will expire in 13d : 23hr : 58m') and warned that the codes expire when the trial ends: something to plan for before you print anything.

The analytics page showed 1,800 total scans and 1,296 unique scanners on a brand-new account, under the banner 'You're exploring a preview of your future insights'. These are sample figures; our CSV export showed 0 real scans for both codes.
The note field took one line; the second line of our note was lost while typing, and the saved note did not appear in the CSV export.
'Add to Watchlist' was switched on by default for each new code, with a promise of a daily scan notification.
The CSV export kept both QR IDs, destinations and names, including the Unicode characters in our second title. Bulk Upload carried a paid-plan crown, so we did not test bringing the file back in.
not_tested: Checkout, tax and the price after the trial
Bulk Upload and re-importing the CSV
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
